tagline: A quarter hour across the island where a colony went missing.
intro: The road comes off the Manns Harbor bridge onto Roanoke Island and follows old US 64 across it, through Manteo to the Washington Baum Bridge, which points toward Nags Head. It is 6.8 miles, a fifteen-minute drive.

In 1587 about 120 men, women and children settled here. Their governor, John White, sailed home for supplies and could not get back until 1590, and by then the colony was gone. He found the word CROATOAN carved into a post. Two island towns carry the names of Manteo and Wanchese, the native men who had gone to London with the English in 1584.

moments.title: Fort Raleigh National Historic Site
moments.text: The colony's own ground, just off US 64 at the north end of the island, where Paul Green's The Lost Colony opened in the Waterside Theatre on July 4, 1937.

moments.title: Manteo
moments.text: County seat since 1870, a port town whose docks began to decline once the 1924 bridge to Nags Head made the road the center of trade.

moments.title: Roanoke Island Festival Park
moments.text: Across the bridge from the Manteo waterfront lies the Elizabeth II, a 69-foot three-masted barque launched in 1983 and named for a ship in Raleigh's 1587 fleet.
